title: Intrinsic derived completion
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring, and $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ a finitely generated ideal. Assume $A/I$ is torsion as an additive group and each $A/I^n$ for $n\geq1$ is finite and perfect over $A$. Use the small pro-etale site, the completed coefficient sheaf $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_T$, and the category $D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\Mod(A_T))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The action of $a_j$ on $A_T$ is induced by its compatible residues in $A/I^n$. Let $K\in D(\Mod(A_T))$ and let $C$ be a cochain complex representing it.

For $m\geq1$, let

$$
 Q_m=K(A_T;a_1^m,\dots,a_r^m)
   =\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^m}A_T]
$$

in cohomological degrees $[-r,0]$. For each factor define a chain map

$$
 [A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^{m+1}}A_T]
 \longrightarrow[A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^m}A_T]
$$

whose degree $-1$ component is multiplication by $a_j$ and whose degree $0$
component is the identity. Their tensor product is a chain map
$q_{m+1,m}:Q_{m+1}\to Q_m$; the composites $q_{m+2,m}=q_{m+1,m}q_{m+2,m+1}$
make $(Q_m)_m$ a strict tower.

Use the total sheaf tensor complex of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] to set $M_m(C)=C\otimes_{A_T}Q_m$, with transitions $t_m=1_C\otimes q_{m+1,m}$. This is a strict tower of complexes, hence a complex in $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Define the product complex $B(C)=\prod_{m\geq1}M_m(C)$ termwise and the chain map
$$
 f_C:B(C)\longrightarrow B(C),\qquad (z_m)_m\longmapsto(z_m-t_mz_{m+1})_m.
$$
Countable products are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] and represent derived products by [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core]. Define a cochain complex $F(C)$ by
$$
 F(C)^i=B(C)^i\oplus B(C)^{i-1},\qquad
 d_{F(C)}^i(x,y)=(d_Bx,f_Cx-d_By).
$$
This is the explicit mapping-fiber model for the sequential derived inverse limit of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. Define $K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$ to be its image in $D(\Mod(A_T))$; thus the notation
$$
 K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}=\Rlim_m(C\otimes_{A_T}Q_m)
$$
uses this specified complex model.

Let $\iota_m:A_T[0]\to Q_m$ be the inclusion in degree zero, and let $u_C:C\to B(C)$ have components $1_C\otimes\iota_m$. Define the completion map $\eta_K:K\to K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$ as the image of the chain map
$$
 C\longrightarrow F(C),\qquad c\longmapsto(u_C(c),0).
$$
Call $K$ derived $I$-complete if $\eta_K$ is an isomorphism. These constructions are read on the derived category by inverting quasi-isomorphisms of representatives, using the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For constant coefficients on an arbitrary site $\mathcal C$, Stacks Tag 099M (proetale.tex, lemma-naive-completion), in Tag 099L (section-derived-completion-noetherian), identifies derived completion for a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with $R\lim_n(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$. That theorem is context for the definition; comparison of the completed-coefficient Koszul tower above with the completed-coefficient quotient tower is a separate assertion, not part of this definition.

proof.text: The exterior power of the diagonal generator map commutes with Koszul contraction. Its zeroth exterior power fixes the coefficient unit. The total-tensor summand formula and naturality of the right unitor show that the tensor units are compatible with the tower transitions. By the product universal property their composite with one minus shift is zero, proving completedKoszulLift_relation with zero homotopy. The tensor-unit differential, transition and naturality calculations are proved abstractly in an additive monoidal category, then specialized, so no change to the concrete tensor definitions is needed.

The cohomologically reindexed Koszul complex is bounded above by zero and its terms are projective exterior powers, hence flat. Apply the module bounded-above flat K-flat criterion, then the constant-realization K-flat clause and preservation of K-flatness by ordinary coefficient extension. Tensoring a quasi-isomorphism with the resulting complex is a quasi-isomorphism, by the tensor/mapping-cone isomorphism.

Define the tensor maps, their product maps, and the arrow functor of minus one-minus-shift. Exact countable products imply exact discrete-natural limits, so the limit of the tensor quasi-isomorphisms is a quasi-isomorphism. The morphism of mapping-cone distinguished triangles and the two-out-of-three lemma show that its mapping-cone map is a quasi-isomorphism. Shifting by minus one gives the explicit mapping-fiber functor.

Naturality of the tensor units gives naturality of the product unit. Compute the zero-homotopy cocone lift on each term using the cocone biproduct identity. Naturality of the cone map then proves naturality of completedKoszulUnitComplex. Localize the fiber functor and this natural transformation by Localization.lift and Localization.liftNatTrans. The canonical factorization isomorphism cancels its inverse to give exactly the required equation for the descended unit.

blueprint_update.statement:
For $m\geq1$, let

$$
 Q_m=K(A_T;a_1^m,\dots,a_r^m)
   =\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^m}A_T]
$$

in cohomological degrees $[-r,0]$. For each factor define a chain map

$$
 [A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^{m+1}}A_T]
 \longrightarrow[A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^m}A_T]
$$

whose degree $-1$ component is multiplication by $a_j$ and whose degree $0$
component is the identity. Their tensor product is a chain map
$q_{m+1,m}:Q_{m+1}\to Q_m$; the composites $q_{m+2,m}=q_{m+1,m}q_{m+2,m+1}$
make $(Q_m)_m$ a strict tower.

For a functorial K-flat representative $QK$, the complexes
$QK\otimes_{A_T}Q_m$ form an object of $D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. Define

$$
 K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}
   =\Rlim_m(QK\otimes_{A_T}Q_m).
$$

The compatible degree-zero maps $A_T\to Q_m$ define $K\to
K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$. The object $K$ is derived $I$-complete if this
map is an isomorphism.
